claims.text: A W–Ta–Cr–V–Hf refractory high-entropy alloy is a suitable example of the proposed tungsten-based alloy system.
Mechanical alloying and sintering can produce the proposed alloy with a single-phase matrix.
Controlled post-sintering annealing can induce nanoscale coherent nanoprecipitates in a tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy.
The annealing treatment can make the coherent nanoprecipitates uniformly distributed throughout the matrix.

Ar+ irradiation at 150 keV and approximately 2.4 × 10^20 at/m^2, together with He+ at 10 keV and D+ at 5 keV, is applicable to irradiation testing of tungsten-containing refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed irradiation benefit should hold at approximately 800°C.
Coherent nanoprecipitates capture irradiation-generated vacancies and interstitials and thereby act as efficient defect sinks.
Capture of vacancies and interstitials by the nanoprecipitates increases defect recombination.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Facilitated dislocation transmission and relief of stress concentrations can preserve strength and ductility.
The optimized annealed alloy will exhibit more than a 50% reduction in void density relative to the as-sintered baseline after irradiation.
The optimized annealed alloy will retain yield strength and ductility better than the as-sintered baseline after irradiation.
The as-sintered baseline will display higher void swelling and greater mechanical degradation under irradiation than the optimized annealed alloy.
Annealing or thermal exposure can cause phase growth and microstructural instability in tungsten-containing refractory high-entropy alloys.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency will limit the irradiation-tolerance and mechanical benefits.
Large deviations in irradiation temperature or dose may limit the proposed improvement.
The long-term stability of the nanoprecipitates under extended irradiation remains uncertain.
A controlled comparison of annealed and as-sintered samples can measure void density, precipitate morphology, yield strength, and ductility after identical irradiation.
